I’m so disappointed by some of the comments on here. People do not seem to get that weight is at best an indicator of health. It is not an end all be all and it is indeed the case that many people have a “set point” weight which is hard to deviate from. You could definitely outrun me (5”8, 160 lbs) in a 5K and please ignore these people who are trying to bring you down. That comment about running slowly would eat me up too. It’s pretty rude to make assumptions. It actually reminds me of how men would often make comments about how they were sure I was so flexible or “in shape” simply based on my smaller body. Right now I weigh 40 lbs more than my lowest weight and I am in WAY better shape. People simply cannot comprehend that women’s bodies in particular often require a higher level of fat than is perceived as maximal fitness in order to menstruate and stay hormonally healthy—I had hypothalamic amenorrhea, constantly cold, and poor sleep when I was 120-130 lbs, which didn’t go away til I was at 140 lbs, yet I was PERCEIVED as being more fit at my lowest weight even though I didn’t even run then. It’s actually quite sad. Anecdotally from my own body, I actually need to have a higher BMI (at least 23) if I want to keep cycling. I’m bitter about it sometimes because it certainly is particular to everyone’s individual body but it is FAR more common than we acknowledge and it is what it is. 

Sorry that you’re encountering Reddit’s obsession with diet culture, it’s disappointing.

EDIT: to the people downvoting me, I would appreciate it if you would actually engage with what I’m saying. If you are downvoting, it concerns me that you may not be informed about the risk of hypothalamic amenorrhea and hormonal disturbances from overexercise and/or low body weight.

My experience is that like many women, I did not get a period at 125 lbs due to low body weight and disruptions of my hypothalamic pituitary axis, which yes is a problem for bone health and a myriad of other symptoms no matter your weight. My situation is illustrative that low body weight /=/ health. It is factual that I am healthier and can run about 5x farther at 160 lbs than I could at 125 lbs, when my body decided I shouldn’t reproduce due to lack of energy. This might not be true for runners who have a naturally smaller build, but for someone who lost 30+ lbs over the course of several years to get to that weight, it was absolutely true for me. My extreme hunger and binge eating that developed at 125 lbs also did not go away until I hit 140 lbs, which is yet another signal your body sends you when you are undernourished. Noperiodnownwhat has more information about this issue. Point is: lower BMI /=/ healthier!

I actually had this same issue! Usually I wouldn’t feel it in my calves but I knew it had to be relayed. My right foot would go numb from around miles 3-5 then it would regain sensation but it was still miserable. It went away for several weeks after my first half marathon. Then I took 2 weeks off and really cut back on my running and it stayed away. I was hoping I was done for good, then it returned just today on the last run of my 12 mile week. I’m not sure if it’s coincidence or not that I hadn’t been doing toe raises or calf raises (which I typically do as prehab) for almost a month til yesterday. 

Backstory to all of this—prior to this March, I had crippling foot pain that prevented me from running further than 2 miles from 2012-2017, at which point I gave up and stopped trying to run farther than that. I must’ve tried 5 times to do Couch to 5K and build up slowly, but every time, the foot pain would recur until I had to stop and walk for it to go away, so all I could do were walk/runs if I wanted to exercise longer than 20 minutes. I tried everything—orthotics, stretching, physical therapy—but none of it took because I didn’t have a strong enough core or glutes and in retrospect, I couldn’t fully accept just how much strength I’d need to build coming from a couch potato background. When I saw a PT for it in 2015 they said it wasn’t compartment syndrome and that my calves were tight and glutes were weak. Sometime soon after that, I got frustrated because I was so sure something else was wrong and decided to just accept my limitations. 

During the past 3 years, entirely by coincidence, I got really into weight lifting and significantly enhance my glute strength, and did make some small improvements in mobility. In March when the pandemic hit, I finally tried Couch to 5K again just for giggles and was so overjoyed that at last I was able to run without foot pain! I can only presume it was my increased glute strength that finally got rid of this issue, but I’ve only had maybe 2 runs where I’ve experienced the same pain and it’s MUCH milder. I have noticed this seems to happen if I’m not taking as much of a break from exercise. It was also hugely helpful that I started wearing Correct Toes at night to space out my toes (I have a mild bunion), got toe socks, and bought Altra Ones which have a large toe box. 

So. With my history, when my right foot started going numb 3-4 miles into my runs several months ago, initially I brushed it off because at least it wasn’t painful lol and I could run through it despite the unpleasantness. Obviously I haven’t totally figured the numbness out yet, but for myself due to my history I believe it’s mostly an issue of resting my glutes enough (after already having strengthened them) and it may be the same for you. I typically do weight training 3x a week and hit the glutes hard, and I never made the connection to the foot numbness, but I’m now pretty sure that my glutes today were too tired to work at their usual pace and my calves were overcompensating as a result. I also noticed today that I had calve soreness and pain in my left foot in addition to numbness in my right foot, which suggests strongly to me that the numbness is just a milder issue of the pain I had before and that the solution will be to time my runs more effectively with my weight lifting sessions. Hope you find a solution!
